classification.difficultyReason: Use a three-sided perimeter constraint to form and maximise a quadratic area function.

content.prompt: The council wants to make a rectangular swimming area at the beach using the seashore on one side and 300 m of shark-proof netting for 3 sides. What are the dimensions of the rectangle that encloses the greatest area?

spec.description: Three unlabelled netted sides beneath a light blue shore strip extending beyond both vertical sides. The strip identifies the unnetted side.
spec.mathematics: A rectangular enclosure uses netting on two perpendicular widths and one length.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question diagram; no dimensions or answers supplied.

answer.short: $150$ m along the seashore and $75$ m perpendicular to it; greatest area $11\,250\text{ m}^2$.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ m be each side perpendicular to the shore and $y$ m the side parallel to it.
$$\begin{aligned}2x+y&=300\\y&=300-2x\\A(x)&=x(300-2x)\\A(x)&=300x-2x^2,\qquad 0<x<150\\A'(x)&=300-4x.\end{aligned}$$
Setting $A'(x)=0$ gives $x=75$.
$$\begin{aligned}A''(x)&=-4<0\\y&=300-2(75)=150\\A(75)&=75(150)=11\,250.\end{aligned}$$
The quadratic opens downwards, so this is the global maximum. The dimensions are $150$ m along the shore and $75$ m perpendicular to it, giving an area of $11\,250\text{ m}^2$.
